question: Can constraining the loaded rise to downward modeled motion at every foot avoid the immediate support loss observed after all 44 R10AA rise commands?

change_scope.support_establishment: Preserve the R10AA native-qualified load-seeking law exactly.
change_scope.weak_support_during_raise: Preserve R10AA load seeking when any original native-qualified foot condition is false.
change_scope.loaded_raise: Search the original finite measured-pose candidate grid with an additional all-foot downward-direction constraint.
change_scope.terminal: No controller command after the original terminal transition.

loaded_rise_constraint.inequality: For every foot, foot(target_joints, measured_torso).y - foot(measured_joints, measured_torso).y <= -0.25 * virtual_translation_world_y + 1e-12

refusal: If no cost-decreasing candidate satisfies the joint, lateral and downward-foot constraints, return an explicit bounded hold without rewriting observations, phase clocks or task limits.
validation_required: Reproduce the 44 retained loaded-rise reference plans before interpreting the counterfactual model.
Check the prospective compiled search on all 646 exposed observations with original inputs preserved; controller admission remains separate from model feasibility.
Prove exact R10AA behavior for support seeking and weak-support fallback.
Cover terminal, missing/nonfinite/native-unqualified input, no-admissible-candidate and joint-boundary controls.
Use a distinct native profile, composition, runtime binding and source key; preserve older controller behavior.
Complete the applicable safety graph before a freshly declared native diagnostic; offline feasibility never qualifies physics.
design_limits: The fixed-torso constraint describes target direction, not predicted force or guaranteed contact retention.
No held-out population or physical attempt is declared by this kernel contract.
Original standing, readiness, cycle/stop conditions and physical budgets remain unchanged.
